days.label: Day 1 — Arrive & settle
days.summary: Land, drop bags at the hotel and ease in with a gentle riverside evening so small legs aren't overwhelmed on day one.

activities.title: Unpack and a first swim
activities.body: Check in, unpack the allergy kit somewhere everyone can find it, then a short swim to shake off the flight.

activities.title: Riverside walk and dinner
activities.body: An easy walk by the water. Pick a restaurant where you can speak to the kitchen about Pip's tree-nut allergy before ordering.

days.label: Day 2 — Gardens by the Bay
days.summary: The big one: two different adventures at the same place in the morning, a carefully-handled lunch, a rain-proof afternoon, and a quiet swim to finish.
days.did_you_know: The Supertrees are vertical gardens up to 50 metres tall — some collect rainwater and solar energy for the whole park.

star_challenge.title: Explorer of the day
star_challenge.prompt: Find one thing at the Gardens that you've never seen before and tell a grown-up about it.

moments.title: Gardens by the Bay — two adventures, one place

activities.title: Sam's Supertree engineering quest
activities.body: How do you build a tree taller than a building? Walk the OCBC Skyway and work out what holds the Supertrees up.

explorer.body: Count the steel ribs on a Supertree and guess how rainwater travels down inside it. Sketch your own giant tree that could power a house.
explorer.fact: Each Supertree trunk is a concrete core wrapped in a steel frame that real plants grow up.

quiz.q: What two things do some Supertrees collect from the sky?

facts: The tallest Supertree is about 50 metres — roughly a 16-storey building.

challenge.prompt: How tall is the tallest Supertree, roughly?

activities.title: Pip's Hidden Creatures trail (Cloud Forest)
activities.body: Step inside the misty mountain and hunt for hidden animals among the waterfalls and ferns.

little.body: Can you find the big waterfall, a tiny frog and a sparkly flower? Point to each one and give it a name.
little.fact: The Cloud Forest waterfall is one of the tallest indoor waterfalls in the world.

quiz.q: What falls down inside the Cloud Forest?

moments.title: Lunch at Satay by the Bay

activities.title: Hawker lunch — Pip's tree-nut allergy flagged
activities.body: Tree-nut allergy: flagged. Satay sauce is made from ground peanuts and some stalls also use tree nuts, so this stop needs a kitchen check before ordering. What we checked: this is an open hawker centre with many stalls, so cross-contact is possible. Confirm on the day: ask each stall directly and watch for shared utensils. Lower-risk choices: grilled chicken rice, plain noodles or fresh fruit from stalls that do not prepare satay sauce. Higher-risk: any satay stall and its peanut/nut sauces. The final call always stays with a grown-up.

safety.note: Pip has a serious tree-nut allergy. Satay sauce is peanut/nut based. Use the ask-the-kitchen card, keep the EpiPen on you, and confirm with each stall before ordering — we flag and remind, we never say a dish is safe.

activities.title: Ask-the-kitchen card (English + Mandarin)
activities.body:
Show this to the stall before ordering.

English: "Does this dish contain any nuts or nut oils? My daughter has a serious tree-nut allergy."

中文: "这道菜含有坚果或坚果油吗？我女儿对坚果严重过敏。"

If the stall is unsure, treat it as a no and choose another dish.

activities.title: Indoor anchor if the afternoon storm rolls in
activities.body: Heavy showers are common after lunch. This is your pre-loaded indoor backup: the Future World digital playground is hands-on for both a 6 and a 9 year old. Swap it in if the radar looks wet — no re-planning needed.

activities.title: Pool wind-down and keepsake page
activities.body: An easy swim, then a few minutes for the kids to add to their keepsake journal while the day is fresh.

days.label: Day 3 — Sentosa
days.summary: Cable car across to Sentosa, beach time and a gentle nature walk, with the same allergy routine at lunch.

activities.title: Ride over the harbour
activities.body: Glass cabins with big views — great for spotting ships and counting cranes.

activities.title: Sandcastle and shell hunt
activities.body: Build, dig and hunt for the prettiest shell. Reapply sunscreen — it's strong here.

days.label: Day 4 — River Wonders & home
days.summary: A relaxed final morning with the animals before the flight home.

activities.title: Find the manatees and pandas
activities.body: A calm last adventure — spot the giant pandas and the gentle manatees before heading to the airport.

grownups.essentials: Allergy protocol (Pip — tree nuts): carry two adrenaline auto-injectors (EpiPen) at all times, plus antihistamine. Know the signs of a reaction and the plan: give adrenaline first, then call 995 (Singapore emergency). Use the ask-the-kitchen card at every meal and confirm with staff before ordering — Yaycay flags and reminds; the final check is always yours. Nearest hospital to Marina Bay: Singapore General Hospital.
checklist: Pack 2x EpiPen + antihistamine in the day bag
Show the ask-the-kitchen card before ordering at every stall
Confirm tree-nut handling with staff — don't rely on the menu alone
Carry water and sunscreen; reapply after the pool and beach
Save 995 (emergency) and the hotel address in your phone
grownups.transport: Singapore is easy on the MRT and by taxi/Grab. Marina Bay attractions are walkable from the hotel; use Grab when it's raining or legs are tired. Tap an EZ-Link or contactless card for the MRT.
